# CRM Relational-Integrity Inventory — Baseline

**Plan reference:** `docs/plans/crm-relational-integrity-remediation-plan.md`, section 7
("Data migration and quarantine") and Phase 0 ("Run the integrity inventory and
preserve its results").

**Date generated:** 2026-07-31
**Generated by:** Phase 0 containment tooling task (read-only inventory build)

---

## 1. What was built

A read-only diagnostic reducer, `crm_integrity_inventory`, in
`spacetimedb/src/crm/integrity_inventory.rs`, registered via
`spacetimedb/src/crm/mod.rs` (`pub mod integrity_inventory;`).

### Why a reducer, not a `cargo test` binary or `spacetime sql` script

This repo's existing integrity-check precedent
(`spacetimedb/tests/accounting/relational_integrity_test.rs`,
`spacetimedb/tests/proposals/convert_integrity_test.rs`) is not a normal Rust
`#[test]` suite. Per this project's own tooling notes, native `cargo test`/
`cargo build` cannot link against the SpacetimeDB WASM host bindings — only
`cargo check` succeeds natively. The existing pattern instead compiles test
logic directly into the WASM module as ordinary functions, wrapped by
`#[spacetimedb::reducer]` entry points declared in `tests/<domain>/mod.rs`
files that are pulled into `src/lib.rs` via `#[path = "../tests/..."]`, and
run with `spacetime call <db> run_all_<domain>_tests`.

The integrity inventory follows the same idiom, because it is the only
mechanism in this codebase that can iterate real persisted `ctx.db` tables:
it is a reducer, callable the same way. The differences from the test-suite
precedent:

- It lives under `src/crm/` (not `tests/crm/`) because it is a permanent
  operational diagnostic meant to be re-run against real environments, not a
  disposable test fixture that seeds its own throwaway `OrgFixture` data.
- It performs **zero writes**. It never calls `.insert()`, `.update()`, or
  `.delete()` on any table — only `.iter()` / index reads. This was verified
  by inspection: every table handle in the file is read via `.iter()` and
  every collected value is a `u64` id pushed into a `Vec`, `HashMap`, or
  `HashSet` for local computation.
- Findings are reported via `log::info!`/`log::warn!` (one line per category,
  each carrying the category name, a violation count, and up to 5 sample row
  IDs) rather than `Result::Err`, because a reducer cannot return data to the
  caller (CLAUDE.md core concept: "reducers do not return data to callers").
  The report is read back with `spacetime logs <db>`.

### How to run it

```bash
# Against a local dev database:
spacetime start                         # if not already running
spacetime publish <db-name> --module-path spacetimedb   # deploy the updated module
spacetime call <db-name> crm_integrity_inventory
spacetime logs <db-name> | grep "\[crm-integrity\]"

# Against maincloud (only once ready to check real tenant data; the report
# is read-only and safe, but follow this repo's normal maincloud deployment
# review process before publishing there):
spacetime publish <db-name>              # server defaults to maincloud per spacetime.json
spacetime call <db-name> crm_integrity_inventory
spacetime logs <db-name> | grep "\[crm-integrity\]"
```

Re-run after each remediation phase (CRM-RI-001 through CRM-RI-017) lands to
confirm violation counts, especially for P0-linked categories, have dropped
to zero (plan section 7, item 7).

## 2. What it checks

The reducer runs nine independent checks, one per plan section 7 item 5
category, over the following tables: `contact`, `contact_relationship`,
`contact_tag`/`contact_tag_assignment`, `contact_category`/
`contact_category_assignment`, `contact_phone_identity`, `lead`,
`lead_source`, `lead_lost_reason`, `opportunity`, `opp_stage`,
`opportunity_line`, `crm_conversation`, `crm_conversation_message`,
`contact_segment`, `segment_member`, and `sale_order` (the CRM → Sales
cross-reference for opportunity conversion).

| # | Category | What is detected |
|---|----------|-------------------|
| 1 | `zero_and_missing_ids` | Relation fields holding sentinel `0` instead of `None`/a real ID: `contact.parent_id`; `lead.source_id`/`campaign_id`/`team_id`/`partner_id`/`lost_reason_id`; `opportunity.stage_id`/`lead_id`/`partner_id`/`contact_id`/`lost_reason_id`; `opportunity_line.opportunity_id`/`product_id`; `sale_order.opportunity_id` |
| 2 | `dangling_relations` | Each FK-like field above (plus `contact_relationship`, `contact_phone_identity.contact_id`, `crm_conversation.contact_id`/`phone_identity_id`, `crm_conversation_message.conversation_id`, `segment_member.segment_id`/`contact_id`, `contact_tag_assignment`, `contact_category_assignment`) whose target row is absent from the target table |
| 3 | `cross_org_company` | `contact.parent_id`, `lead.partner_id`, `opportunity.partner_id`/`contact_id`, `sale_order.opportunity_id`/`partner_id`, and `contact_phone_identity.company_id` where the referenced row belongs to a different `organization_id` or `company_id` than the referencing row |
| 4 | `deleted_or_merged_contact_targets` | Any live (non-deleted) relation — contact parent, lead partner, opportunity partner/contact, active `contact_relationship`, `crm_conversation`, active `segment_member`, `sale_order.partner_id` — still pointing at a contact with `deleted_at.is_some()` or `merge_target_id.is_some()` |
| 5 | `contradictory_opportunity_state` | `opportunity.is_won && is_lost` both true, or `is_won` true while the linked `opp_stage.is_won` is false (CRM-RI-011) |
| 6 | `duplicate_sales_orders_per_opportunity` | More than one `sale_order` row sharing the same non-null `opportunity_id` (CRM-RI-005) |
| 7 | `contact_hierarchy_cycles` | `contact.parent_id` chains that loop back to an ancestor instead of terminating (CRM-RI-006) |
| 8 | `duplicate_associations_and_stale_counts` | Duplicate `(contact_id, tag_id)` / `(contact_id, category_id)` / active `(segment_id, contact_id)` rows, and `contact_segment.member_count` values that disagree with the live count of active `segment_member` rows |
| 9 | `forged_identity_verification` | `contact_phone_identity` rows marked `Verified` with no `verified_at` timestamp, or whose `company_id` does not match the owning contact's `company_id` (CRM-RI-008, evidence near `contact_identities.rs:225`) |

## 3. Execution status: NOT YET RUN against real data

**This tool has not been executed against a populated database.** No results
below are fabricated; this section documents exactly what was attempted and
why it could not complete in this environment, so whoever has proper
credentials can finish the run.

### What was verified

- `cargo check` passes cleanly for the whole workspace with the new module
  included (native build; WASM link is a separate step handled by
  `spacetime publish`, consistent with this repo's documented tooling
  behavior).
- `spacetime publish -s local lumiere-v1-j1uo0 --module-path ./spacetimedb -y`
  (updating this environment's one existing local database, which contains
  only synthetic data from this repo's own domain test-harness reducers —
  e.g. log lines show `run_all_accounting_tests` seeding rows named `Harness
  Goods …` — not production data) **failed**:
  ```
  Error: Pre-publish check failed with status 403 Forbidden:
  c2005afd51914e8402e3063946fc2d00e073ec76bf962b2161da27da4c93af82 is not
  authorized to perform action on database
  c200dbaf9baf8f222ea8c527c0f2a9c3d2741982dcdd5e886b7166e93a3f1b4a: update database
  ```
  The active `spacetime login` identity in this sandbox
  (`c2005afd51914e8402e3063946fc2d00e073ec76bf962b2161da27da4c93af82`) is not
  the owner of that database.
- Publishing a brand-new local database under a fresh name (tried
  `crm-integrity-check` and `testinventorydb`) also failed:
  ```
  Error: No database target matches '<name>'. Available databases: lumiere-v1-j1uo0
  ```
  This local SpacetimeDB instance only recognizes the one pre-existing
  database and does not allow creating a new one from this identity in this
  sandbox.
- Per task constraints, publishing to maincloud was intentionally not
  attempted — that would touch a real hosted database outside this
  containment task's scope.

### Net result

No CRM tables in this environment could be scanned. Every category above
returned **no data, not zero** — "zero violations" is a real result this
tool can produce, but it has not yet been produced here. Do not read the
absence of numbers in section 2 as "clean"; it means "unrun."

### How to complete this run

Whoever has publish rights on either an existing dev/staging SpacetimeDB
database or a fresh local one should:

1. `spacetime publish <db-name> --module-path spacetimedb` (add `--clear-database`
   only if starting fresh; do **not** clear a database with data you want to
   inventory).
2. `spacetime call <db-name> crm_integrity_inventory`
3. `spacetime logs <db-name> | grep "\[crm-integrity\]"`
4. Paste the nine `[crm-integrity] category=... count=... sample_ids=...` log
   lines (plus the start/done summary line) into section 2's table (or below
   it) of this document, replacing this section, and note the database/
   environment name and date.
5. Re-run after each remediation phase per plan section 7, item 7.

## 4. Constraints honored

- The reducer is read-only: no `insert`/`update`/`delete` calls anywhere in
  `integrity_inventory.rs`.
- No CRM issues were fixed as part of this task — this is inventory tooling
  only, per the plan's Phase 0/Phase 1 split.
- No production/maincloud database was touched or queried.
- No results were fabricated; section 3 documents the actual attempt and
  actual errors encountered.
